title: R2-SEC0: burnOnRead/receiptSharing interaction is wrong
description: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md line 513: The burnOnRead fix states 'When the recipient's effective receiptSharing preference is false, no readAt signal will reach the sender; burnOnRead is not guaranteed to trigger in that case.' This is factually incorrect and introduces a confidentiality hazard. burnOnRead deletion occurs on the RECEIVER's mailbox when the receiver's LOCAL readAt is set. receiptSharing controls only whether an outbound Peer/receipt call is made to the sender's server; it does not suppress the receiver's own local readAt write. Therefore burnOnRead DOES trigger when receiptSharing=false, because the receiver's local readAt is always set when the user reads the message. The fix conflates 'the sender does not receive a Peer/receipt notification' with 'burnOnRead does not trigger' — these are independent events. An implementer reading this text could incorrectly skip the burnOnRead hard-delete when receiptSharing=false, causing the message to persist when it should have been deleted, which is a confidentiality failure. Correct statement: burnOnRead triggers unconditionally on the receiver's mailbox when local readAt is set; receiptSharing=false means the sender is not notified (via Peer/receipt) that the message was read, but the deletion still occurs.
close_reason: Fixed: burnOnRead text corrected — hard-delete fires normally; sender just can't confirm (chat-00.md:513)
